raw_response:
I farm the same 9 mu in the usual wheat-maize rotation, so I will not change too much this year. At my age, I do not like gambling on new methods unless I see them work nearby. I will follow what has worked on my land and what the neighbors with good harvests are doing, then adjust a little because fertilizer, seed, water, and spray all cost money. Since I have well irrigation, I can push yield a bit more steadily, so I would rather not let the crop go hungry. For wheat, I will use an improved variety like the ones people around here have been planting, put more fertilizer into the base and then topdress nitrogen after it turns green and again around jointing, with 3 irrigations if the weather is normal. For maize, I will use hybrid seed, keep the stand even, put enough nitrogen because maize eats heavily, and use 2 irrigations if rainfall is not enough. I do not chase fancy things. I do solid tillage, enough fertilizer, timely water, and 2 sprays per crop so I do not lose yield at a key time.
